cues.text: Good morning. What can I do for you?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: I want to report a theft. I had some things stolen out of my bag yesterday.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: I’m sorry to hear that. Right, so I’ll need to take a few details. Can I start with your name?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Louise Taylor.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: OK, thank you. And are you resident in the UK?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: No, I’m actually Canadian. Though my mother was British.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: And your date of birth?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: December 14th, 1977.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: So you’re just visiting this country?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: That’s right. I come over most summers on business. I’m an interior designer and I come over to buy old furniture, antiques you know. There are some really lovely things around here, but you need to get out to the small towns. I’ve had a really good trip this year, until this happened.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: OK. So you’ve been here quite a while?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Yes, I’m here for two months. I go back next week.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: So may I ask where you’re staying now?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Well at present I’ve got a place at Park Apartments, that’s on King Street. I was staying at the Riverside Apartments on the same street, but the apartment there was only available for six weeks so I had to find another one.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: OK. And the apartment number?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Fifteen.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Now, I need to take some details of the theft. So you said you had some things stolen out of your bag?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: That’s right.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: And were you actually carrying the bag when the theft took place?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Yes, I really can’t understand it. I had my backpack on. And I went into a supermarket to buy a few things and when I opened it up my wallet wasn’t there.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: And what did your wallet have in it?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Well, fortunately I don’t keep my credit cards in that wallet – I keep them with my passport in an inside compartment in my backpack. But there was quite a bit of cash there … about £250 sterling, I should think. I withdrew £300 from my account yesterday, but I did a bit of shopping, so I must have already spent about £50 of that.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: OK.
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: At first I thought, oh I must have left the wallet back in the apartment, but then I realised my phone had gone as well. It was only a week old, and that’s when I realised I’d been robbed. Anyway at least they didn’t take the keys to my rental car.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Yes. So you say the theft occurred yesterday?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: So that was September the tenth. And do you have any idea at all of where or when the things might possibly have been stolen?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Well at first I couldn’t believe it because the bag had been on my back ever since I left the apartment after lunch. It’s just a small backpack, but I generally use it when I’m travelling because it seems safer than a handbag. Anyway, I met up with a friend, and we spent a couple of hours in the museum. But I do remember that as we were leaving there, at about 4 o’clock, a group of young boys ran up to us, and they were really crowding round us, and they were asking us that time it was, then all of a sudden they ran off.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Can you remember anything about them?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: The one who did most of the talking was wearing a T-shirt with a picture of something … let’s see … a tiger.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Right. Any idea of how old he might have been?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Around twelve years old?
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: And can you remember anything else about his appearance?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Not much. He was quite thin …
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Colour of hair?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: I do remember that – he was blond. All the others were dark-haired.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: And any details of the others?
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Not really. They came and went so quickly.
cues.speaker: LOUISE

cues.text: Right. So what I’m going to do now is give you a crime reference number so you can contact your insurance company. So this is ten digits: 87954 82361
cues.speaker: OFFICER

cues.text: Thank you. So should I …
cues.speaker: LOUISE
